text: The next two questions relate to the term ‘isotope’. a. Using an example, explain what is meant by the term ‘isotope’. [2] b. Would you expect two isotopes of the same element to have similar or different chemical properties? Explain your answer. [2]
html:
The next two questions relate to the term ‘isotope’.

a. Using an example, explain what is meant by the term ‘isotope’. [2]

b. Would you expect two isotopes of the same element to have similar or

different chemical properties? Explain your answer. [2]
answerHtml:
2. The next two questions relate to the term ‘isotope’.

a. Using an example, explain what is meant by the term ‘isotope’. [2]

Atoms with the same number of protons as one another but different numbers of neutrons.

Any valid example: e.g C-14 has 6 protons, 8 neutrons, wheras C-12 had 6 protons, and 6 neutrons;

(Not sufficient to just give the examples, e.g. C-14, but not refer to the number of neutrons)

b. Would you expect two isotopes of the same element to have similar or

different chemical properties? Explain your answer. [2]

Similar chemical properties as it is the number of valence electrons which determines the chemical properties of an element
